Q: Thanks for taking the time to talk with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you reported.
Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just give you the facts, if that's okay. I'm not feeling great.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me wehre the collision happened and what you were doing just before it?
A: It was in Baytown, Texas, on a two-lane road near a shopping center. I was driving home from work, going maybe
twenty-five miles an hour because the road was wet.
Q: Which direction were you traveling, and what happened next?
A: I was heading east. The other car came over into my lane. We hit head-on, but it wasn't a hard hit. Honestly it felt
more like a bump, though my head snapped forward and back.
Q: Did your airbags deploy?
A: I don't think so. The steering wheel didn't hit me hard, but I hit my head on the side window.
Q: Did you lose consciousness, even briefly?
A: I don't think I blacked out, but everything went foggy for a few seconds. I got out of the car and sat on the curb.
Q: Have you sought medical attention since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to the emergency room. They said I have a concussion. I've got a headache, I'm sensitive to light, and
I'm having trouble concentrating. The doctor told me to rest and avoid screens as much as I can.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add about the collision?
A: Just that I'm still pretty dizzy, so if I seem slow answering, that's why.
Q: Understood. We'll follow up once we have your medical records. Thank you for your time.
</page>
